questions.stem: A 15-year-old with dyspnea, cough, and wheezing. The physician suggested RAST for diagnosis. What is the likely disease?
questions.solutionHtml:
Asthma

RAST or Radioallergosorbent tests, which can detect the presence of IgE antibodies that are specific for individual allergens, are used for the diagnosis of Asthma.



Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 679

questions.stem: A woman after taking aspirin suddenly started wheezing. Which of the following is not true regarding this condition?

options.label: A
options.text: Negative skin test for inhaled allergen

questions.solutionHtml:
Raised serum IgE levels
  • The given clinical scenario with aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease (AERD), also known as Samter's triad.
  • It is a type of intrinsic asthma that is triggered by the ingestion of aspirin or other nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and is often associated with nasal polyps.
  • The IgE levels are normal.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 680

questions.stem: A 18-years-old male presents to the emergency department with acute shortness of breath, wheezing, and chest tightness. He has a history of seasonal allergies and eczema since childhood. His vital signs include a respiratory rate of 28 breaths per minute, oxygen saturation of 90% on room air, and a pulse rate of 110 beats per minute. On examination, he has diffuse expiratory wheezing and prolonged expiration. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis for this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Atopic asthma
  • The given clinical scenario with a history of seasonal allergies and eczema is suggestive of atopic asthma.
  • The presenting symptoms of acute shortness of breath, wheezing, and chest tightness, along with physical examination findings of diffuse expiratory wheezing and prolonged expiration, are consistent with an asthma exacerbation.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 682

questions.stem: Increase the level of which compound is associated with airway remodeling, disease severity, and decreased pulmonary function.
questions.solutionHtml:
YKL 40
  • Increased serum levels and lung expression of YKL-40 are correlated with disease severity, airway remodeling, and decreased pulmonary function.
  • YKL-40 is a glycoprotein that is produced by various cells, including macrophages, neutrophils, and epithelial cells, in response to inflammation. It has been implicated in several respiratory diseases, including asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), and bronchiectasis.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 682

questions.stem: Charcot-Leyden crystals are composed of an eosinophil protein called as-
questions.solutionHtml:
Galectin 10

Charcot-Leyden crystals

  • These are elongated, needle-shaped crystals that are often found in the sputum and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid of patients with asthma and other eosinophilic respiratory disorders.
  • The crystals are composed of an eosinophil protein called galectin 10, also known as Charcot-Leyden crystal protein.
  • Galectin 10 is a member of the S-type lectin family and is thought to play a role in eosinophil activation, recruitment, and survival in the airways.



Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 682

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a Histological feature of airway remodeling in asthma?

options.label: B
options.text: Increase in the size of the submucosal glands and number of airway goblet cells

options.label: D
options.text: Hypertrophy and/or hyperplasia of the bronchial wall muscle

questions.solutionHtml:
Decreased vascularity

questions.stemHtml: A 24 -year-old patient presented with on-and-off episodes of respiratory difficulties along with a productive cough for the past 3 to 4 months. A lung biopsy demonstrates the finding shown below. What is the likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Asthma
  • The given clinical scenario and a picture showing Charcot-Leyden crystals in lung biopsy is suggestive of Asthma.
  • Charcot Leyden crystals are eosinophilic and needle-shaped crystals that are commonly found in the sputum or lung tissue of patients with asthma.
  • These crystals are formed from the breakdown of an eosinophil protein called  galectin-10.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 682
